title: Queer History in Berlin - FAQ
subtitle: Opening hours and dates checked on 28 October 2026.

items.q: Where is the gay neighbourhood in Berlin?
items.a: The streets around **Nollendorfplatz in Schöneberg**, above all Motzstraße and Fuggerstraße. It was the centre of the scene in the 1920s, with the Eldorado club on Motzstraße, and it still is today.

items.q: How long does the queer history walk take?
items.a: About **6.7 km** for all seven stops, and two and a half to three hours with short stops, plus an hour if you go into the Schwules Museum. The Schöneberg half, stops 4 to 7, is within 1.5 km.

items.q: When is the Schwules Museum open?
items.a: **Closed on Tuesdays.** Monday, Wednesday and Friday 12:00 to 18:00, Thursday 12:00 to 20:00, Saturday 14:00 to 19:00 and Sunday 14:00 to 18:00. Admission is 10 euros, reduced 5. It is **closed from 3 to 8 November 2026**, and from 9 to 26 November only one exhibition is open.

items.q: Where is the Memorial to Homosexuals Persecuted Under Nazism?
items.a: On **Ebertstraße at the edge of the Tiergarten**, a short walk south of the Brandenburg Gate. It is a grey concrete block by Elmgreen and Dragset, opened on 27 May 2008, with a film playing through a small window. It is outdoors and open at any time.

items.q: What happened to Magnus Hirschfeld's Institute?
items.a: Students and SA men **looted it on 6 May 1933**, and its books were burned four days later on today's Bebelplatz. The building is gone. The riverside path near the site is called **Magnus-Hirschfeld-Ufer**, with a memorial stele and six rainbow calla lilies from 2017.

items.q: What is the pink triangle at Nollendorfplatz?
items.a: A granite plaque on the wall of **U Nollendorfplatz**, put up in 1989. It was the first public memorial to the homosexual victims of the Nazis in a German city. The words mean beaten to death, silenced to death.
West Germany reformed it in **1969** and **repealed it in 1994**. The Nazis had widened it in 1935, and about 53,400 men were convicted under it in the Nazi years.
